2026 Conference

# NeurIPS 2026

The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems

Main: Sydney, Australia Dec 6th - 12th

Satellites: Atlanta, Georgia Dec 9th - 13th Paris, France Dec 9th - 13th

## Latest Announcements

Stay updated with conference news

### Sanctions

We want to speak directly to the concern many of you have expressed, and we owe you a clear explanation of what happened, why it happened, and where we stand now. We understand this situation caused genuine alarm and we take that seriously. In preparing the NeurIPS 2026 handbook, we included a link to a US government sanctions tool that covers a significantly broader set of restrictions than those NeurIPS is actually required to follow. This error was due to miscommunication between the NeurIPS Foundation and our legal team; there was never an intention to restrict participation beyond our mandatory compliance obligations. The responsibility for that error is ours as an organization, and we deeply apologize for the alarm and impact this miscommunication had on our community. We have updated the link and clarified the text of our policy, which is consistent with that of ACM and IEEE, as well as other international conferences and NeurIPS in the past. As in previous years, NeurIPS welcomes submissions from all compliant institutions and individuals. We want to reiterate that NeurIPS is a community-driven event, created by and for the community, and strives to be inclusive. The NeurIPS 2026 organizing committee was particularly saddened to learn of this institutional miscommunication. The organizing committee has taken on the responsibility of running the conference this year with the goal of fostering open communication, knowledge sharing, and global scientific discourse. We thank the community for bringing this issue to our attention and working with us through this situation.

AI Reviewing Experiment

More information on NeurIPS 2026 will be available soon. Please check back for additional details on satellite locations and upcoming calls for papers and submissions details.

## Mission Statement

The Neural Information Processing Systems Foundation is a non-profit corporation whose purpose is to foster the exchange of research advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, principally by hosting an annual interdisciplinary academic conference with the highest ethical standards for a diverse and inclusive community.

## About the Conference

The conference was founded in 1987 and is now a multi-track interdisciplinary annual meeting that includes invited talks, demonstrations, symposia, and oral and poster presentations of refereed papers. Along with the conference is a professional exposition focusing on machine learning in practice, a series of tutorials, and topical workshops that provide a less formal setting for the exchange of ideas.

NeurIPS Newsletter – July 2026 – NeurIPS Blog

# NeurIPS Newsletter – July 2026

Welcome to the July edition of the NeurIPS monthly Newsletter!

The NeurIPS Newsletter aims to provide an easy way to keep up to date with NeurIPS events and planning progress, respond to requests for feedback and participation, and find information about new initiatives. This newsletter will focus on NeurIPS 2026, held in Sydney, Australia, with official Satellites in Atlanta, USA and Paris, France. The conference will be held on the following dates:

- Sydney, Australia: from Sunday, Dec 6th to Saturday, Dec 12th
- Atlanta, USA: from Tuesday Dec 8th to Sunday Dec 13th
- Paris, France: from Wednesday Dec 9th to Sunday Dec 13th

You are receiving this newsletter as per your subscription preferences in your NeurIPS profile. As you prepare to attend NeurIPS, we hope that you will find the following information valuable.

This NeurIPS Newsletter includes:

1. Competition Track Decisions Announced
2. Call for Social Events
3. Clarification on the Rebuttals and Author Discussion
4. Creative AI track deadline Extension
5. Upcoming Workshop Decisions

1. NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track Decisions Announced
2. - The NeurIPS 2026 competition track decisions were announced: the program includes competitions ranging from Scientific AI, Physics, and Engineering, to Healthcare, Biology, and Humanitarian Applications, to Foundation Models, Reasoning and AI Evaluation, to Robotics, Agents and Embodied AI.
- For the details and more information on the decisions, read our blog post: https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/07/28/neurips-2026-competitions-announced/
- For any questions, concerns, or feedback, please contact competition-chairs@neurips.cc
3. NeurIPS 2026 Call for Social Events
4. - NeurIPS is soliciting proposals for social events at NeurIPS 2026. NeurIPS social events are community-led events that help attendees connect, exchange ideas, build collaborations, and create lasting memories beyond the technical program. Whether you’re a first-time organizer or a seasoned community builder, we encourage you to submit your idea by September 5, 2026. Let’s make NeurIPS 2026 an unforgettable experience—together! Learn more and submit your proposal: NeurIPS 2026 Call for Socials.
- For any questions, concerns, or feedback, please contact social-chairs@neurips.cc
5. Clarification on the Rebuttals and Author Discussion
6. - A clarification on the timeframe for rebuttals and author discussion, for all three tracks at NeurIPS 2026.Rebuttals can be posted until August 3rd AOE. This includes any back and forth with the reviewers. The “rebuttal” button and “official comment” button will both be treated equivalently – the difference in terminology between the two is to facilitate discussion during the discussion period on OpenReview. This also means you are allowed to post several comments, with a total of over 10000 characters.Please post your answers to the Area Chair’s initial-meta reviews via a comment from July 28th and by August 3rd, so that reviewers can see it too.We emphasize that the entire period from July 27 through August 3 AOE is time for authors to respond to reviews, including with additional results or other responses to reviewers as applicable. It is your choice how you wish to divide this time into initial rebuttals and subsequent discussion with reviewers and ACs.
7. Creative AI track deadline Extension
8. - To accommodate submissions that may require additional preparation time, the NeurIPS 2026 Creative AI Track is extending its submission deadline by one week, to August 10, 2026, Anywhere on Earth (AoE).For more information, please refer to https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForCreativeAI
9. Upcoming Workshop Decisions
10. - The decisions for the workshops will be posted in early August followed by a blog post – stay tuned!

Hsuan-Tien Lin, Razvan Pascanu, Jean Kossaifi, Aadirupa Saha, Khimya Khetarpal, Feng Liu, Christian Wolf

NeurIPS 2026 General Chairs, Communication Chairs, and Local Communication Chairs

To unsubscribe from the NeurIPS newsletter, unselect the “Subscribe to Newsletter” checkbox in your profile: https://neurips.cc/Profile/subscribe. To update your email preference, visit: https://neurips.cc/FAQ/EmailPreferences.

NeurIPS Newsletter – May 2026 – NeurIPS Blog

# NeurIPS Newsletter – May 2026

Welcome to the May edition of the NeurIPS monthly Newsletter!

The NeurIPS Newsletter aims to provide an easy way to keep up to date with NeurIPS events and planning progress, respond to requests for feedback and participation, and find information about new initiatives. This newsletter will focus on NeurIPS 2026, held in Sydney, Australia, with official Satellites in Atlanta, USA and Paris, France. The conference will be held on the following dates:

- Sydney, Australia: from Sunday, Dec 6th to Saturday, Dec 12th

- Atlanta, USA: from Tuesday Dec 8th to Sunday Dec 13th
- Paris, France: from Wednesday Dec 9th to Sunday Dec 13th

You are receiving this newsletter as per your subscription preferences in your NeurIPS profile. As you prepare to attend NeurIPS, we hope that you will find the following information valuable.

This NeurIPS Newsletter includes:

1. CFP of Machine Learning Reproducibility Challenge (MLRC) 2026
2. Call for Ethics Reviewers
3. Responsible AI (RAI) fields for Evaluations and Datasets (ED) track:
4. Call for Papers: Creative AI Track
5. NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track Reviewing Guidelines
6. Clarification on the Workshop Call for Paris and Atlanta
7. Reminder on Workshop Proposal deadline on June 6th

1. CFP of Machine Learning Reproducibility Challenge (MLRC) 2026NeurIPS is committed to promoting reproducibility, replicability, and generalizability of published claims in its conference and machine learning (ML) conferences/journals. In order to formalize the process further, we are delighted to officially partner with the Machine Learning Reproducibility Challenge (MLRC). In particular, we will experiment with integrating MLRC 2026 as an official track of NeurIPS 2026. MLRC has been the primary venue for publishing reproducibility studies and research over many years, and we are happy to add MLRC as an official track at NeurIPS 2026.To be eligible for MLRC 2026, your reproducibility paper must be accepted as is / with minor revisions to TMLR and must have been submitted to TMLR between June 20, 2025 23:59 AOE and September 30, 2026, 23:59 AOE. Please check our CFP for more details.For more details, please check https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/05/04/mlrc-2026-reproducibility-as-an-official-track-at-neurips/ and feel free to write to the reproducibility chairs at reproducibility-chairs@neurips.cc.
2. Call for Ethics ReviewersEthics in ML research is an important part of ensuring the integrity and impact of scientific work, and NeurIPS 2026 is looking for Ethics Reviewers to support this process. If you are able and willing to participate in the review process, please sign up at this form. Feel free to share this call with your colleagues.Further details on the responsibilities and deadlines can be found here https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/05/12/neurips-2026-call-for-ethics-reviewers/. Please reach out to ethics-review-chairs@neurips.cc for any questions.

1. Responsible AI (RAI) fields for Evaluations and Datasets (ED) track:This year, to improve transparency and responsible use of datasets, we are introducing a new requirement for dataset submissions in the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track: all dataset submissions must now include Responsible AI (RAI) metadata as part of the dataset’s Croissant file. The detailed blog post can be found here: https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/05/04/responsible-ai-metadata-requirements-for-the-evaluations-and-datasets-track-neurips-2026/ For more questions, please see the Evaluations and Datasets Track FAQs.
2. Call for Papers: Creative AI TrackIn its fourth year, and following previous years’ success, NeurIPS 2026 Creative AI Track invites research papers and artworks that explore emerging applications, methods, and critiques of artificial intelligence and machine learning in art, design, and creative practice.Focusing on the theme of Agency, this year’s track asks: how agency emerges, is exercised, is negotiated, and is contested through creative practice with AI. Agency may belong to an artist, a collaborator, a model, an audience, a platform, a community, or even a larger social and technical system, and may be asserted, resisted, constrained, or redistributed. We welcome submissions from artists, designers, creatives, researchers, and critical thinkers who question and explore. More info at https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForCreativeAI. To stay up-to-date with all future announcements, please join our mailing list creativeaiml@googlegroups.com. For other inquiries, please contact creative-ai-chairs@neurips.cc.
3. NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track Reviewing GuidelinesStrong competition should generate scientific insight and lasting community resources, not just a leaderboard. Evaluate proposals as infrastructure for advancing the field, not as research papers. A strong proposal enables scientific progress, provides rigorous and fair evaluation, and delivers lasting community value.Evaluate proposals along the following dimensions:1. Scientific relevance and task2. Data, environments, and resources3. Evaluation protocol4. Logistics and organization5. Ethics and riskRead more details on the call for competition track reviewing guidelines at: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CompetitionReviewerGuideline
4. Clarification on the Workshop Call locationThere is likely some confusion on the location of the accepted workshops, and we already asked workshop proposers to indicate their preferred location in the 3-page main proposal draft: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/WorkshopsGuidance But please note, we do not promise to respect the location; we can only try our best to respect it. Feel free to reach out to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop Chairs workshop-chairs@neurips.cc for any remaining questions.
5. Workshop Proposal deadline on June 6thFollowing up from the last month’s newsletter, as the deadline for workshop proposal submissions approaches (6th June, 2026) for all three venues (Sydney, Paris, Atlanta), we have prepared a Workshop FAQ to address frequently asked questions, such as how to choose a location, etc.The FAQ will be growing along with time, so you are encouraged to keep checking it once in a while for any questions you may have.

We also remind you to please follow the guidelines https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/WorkshopsGuidance or reach out to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop Chairs workshop-chairs@neurips.cc, in case any questions arise.

Hsuan-Tien Lin, Razvan Pascanu, Jean Kossaifi, Aadirupa Saha, Khimya Khetarpal, Feng Liu, Christian Wolf

1. NeurIPS 2026 Official SatellitesFollowing the success of the NeurIPS and NeurIPS-Mexico City pilots in 2025, we are thrilled to announce two official NeurIPS 2026 satellite events for this year! These will be held in Paris, France and Atlanta, USA, respectively, running alongside the main venue in Sydney, Australia.Both satellite events will feature keynotes, oral and poster presentations of accepted NeurIPS 2026 papers, as well as workshops. We are planning tutorials, affinity events, and other elements for the satellite sites and we’ll share more information as planning advances.Wherever you choose to join us, the entire NeurIPS organizing committee is working hard to deliver an outstanding experience for the whole community!Get all the information at neurips.cc
2. Call for PapersNeurIPS 2026 is now accepting submissions as of April 15, 2026. Abstracts are due by May 4th, 2026, with full papers due on May 6th, 2026, Anywhere On Earth (AOE). All authors must have an OpenReview profile when submitting. For more information, please read our call for papers here: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForPapers You can read about the key changes to submissions this year in the handbook: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/MainTrackHandbook, and learn about our new initiative for Strengthening Area Chair Engagement and Calibration at NeurIPS in our blog post: https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/03/23/refining-the-review-cycle-neurips-2026-area-chair-pilot/

4. Main submissions: contribution typesNeurIPS encourages and benefits from a diversity of papers and ideas, which can be developed in many different ways. This year, Main Track submissions can select a Contribution Type, including General, Theory, Use-Inspired, Concept & Feasibility, and Negative Results.More info at https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/ReviewerGuidelines See some concrete examples in the companion blog post: https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/04/16/a-choice-of-contribution-types-at-neurips-2026/

The deadlines are the same as for the main and Papers for Position tracks (PPT), with abstracts due by May 4th, 2026 (AOE), and full papers due on May 6th, 2026 (AOE).Authors are advised to carefully read the call for papers: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForEvaluationsDatasets, as well as our companion blog post, which outlines the changes here: Introducing the Evaluations & Datasets Track at NeurIPS 2026.

Authors are encouraged to read the call for papers and the accompanying blog post. The deadlines are the same as for the main track, with abstracts due by May 4th, 2026 (AOE), and full papers due on May 6th, 2026 (AOE).Call for papers: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForPositionPapers Blog post: What’s new for the Position Paper Track at NeurIPS 2026.

Workshops are one-day events intended to provide an informal, dynamic venue for discussion of work in progress and future directions. Workshop applications are due by June 06, 2026 (AOE). The planning for NeurIPS 2026 has already begun, and we are excited to have joined this year as co-General Chairs for the conference, and to make our contributions to this important meeting in our field’s annual calendar.

NeurIPS is a large conference and its organization continues to be mostly driven by volunteers from our community committed to its success. As we start this process, we hope to have as wide a set of people from which to select as chairs for the conference. Please consider nominating yourself, or someone you know, as an organiser for one of the roles in the conference, or in a generalist role that you think might serve the conference better. Serving as an organiser is a great way to build experience of crafting large scientific meetings and balancing the many tradeoffs involved, helps build new networks, and a great way to give back to the community in a way that is different from reviewing and workshops.

Please send nominations by 28 January 2026 using this form.

We encourage early nominations, as submissions will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We will keep the community informed as plans for this year’s conference continue to take shape, including which existing and new roles will be offered for the 2026 edition. Different roles may involve different levels of workload and time commitments, and detailed expectations will be communicated as appropriate.

The main venue of NeurIPS 2026 will be in Sydney, Australia. Chairs are encouraged, though not required, to participate in person. While chairing is primarily a volunteer role, we aim to provide appropriate financial support, in various forms and subject to budget availability, to facilitate in-person attendance. Further details can be clarified as planning progresses.

# NeurIPS Newsletter – June 2026

Welcome to the June edition of the NeurIPS monthly Newsletter!

The NeurIPS Newsletter aims to provide an easy way to keep up to date with NeurIPS events and planning progress, respond to requests for feedback and participation, and find information about new initiatives. This newsletter will focus on NeurIPS 2026, held in Sydney, Australia, with official Satellites in Atlanta, USA and Paris, France. The conference will be held on the following dates:

- Sydney, Australia: from Sunday, Dec 6th to Saturday, Dec 12th
- Atlanta, USA: from Tuesday Dec 8th to Sunday Dec 13th
- Paris, France: from Wednesday Dec 9th to Sunday Dec 13th

You are receiving this newsletter as per your subscription preferences in your NeurIPS profile. As you prepare to attend NeurIPS, we hope that you will find the following information valuable.

This NeurIPS Newsletter includes:

1. Updates in the Position Paper Track
2. Reminder of Call for Ethics Reviewers
3. Call for Tutorials
4. Call for Affinity Events

1. Updates in the Position Paper Track
2. - The Call for Paper of NeurIPS 2026 Position Paper Track requires papers to be substantially human-written, with AI used only for copy-editing or similar peripheral changes to the main text. The Position Paper Track chairs took a conservative approach, noting that excessive AI use in writing submitted position papers may create risks for peer review, including added verification burden for reviewers and questions about attribution.
- To assess whether authors were largely abiding by this policy, the Position Paper Track chairs partnered with Pangram, under an enterprise-level data agreement ensuring that zero data would be retained. After several independent analyses to verify the model and rule out scenarios with significant false positives, the chairs made the difficult decision to uphold the policy: 178 submissions, or 18.4%, will be desk rejected, while 123 submissions, or 12.7%, will be asked to provide evidence of substantial human engagement or risk desk rejection.
- The blog post lays out the analyses informing this decision and shares the organizers’ perspective.
3. Reminder of Call for Ethics Reviewers
4. - NeurIPS is recruiting Ethics Reviewers for NeurIPS 2026!
- If you have experience critically evaluating potential risks and harms in machine learning research, and can provide thoughtful feedback on broader impacts, please read our Call for Reviewers and consider volunteering as an ethics reviewer. You can also directly volunteer here: NeurIPS 2026 Ethics Reviewer Self-Nomination – Fill out form
- Please share with qualified and interested colleagues! The scale of the conference continues to grow, so we are always seeking to grow our pool of ethics reviewers.
5. Call for Tutorials
6. - NeurIPS is calling proposals for in-person tutorials, please send your proposals before July 3rd, 2026, AOE. Read more about this year’s guidelines here: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForTutorials
- Whether you are planning to send a proposal or not, let us know what topics you would like to see covered in tutorials by filling our survey: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScG3y-x_I_7nd7FOD9kAsiqnhMW8vsLUe9MivTOzgwXoU-E_Q/viewform?usp=header
7. Call for Affinity Events
8. - NeurIPS is calling proposals for affinity events at NeurIPS 2026. Affinity groups interested in organizing an event are invited to submit the Application Form and signed Agreement Form by June 28th, 2026, AOE, to affinity-chairs@neurips.cc.
- For any questions, concerns, or feedback, please contact affinity-chairs@neurips.cc.

NeurIPS 2026 — Sydney — Dec 6-12 26, Sydney · AI What's On Skip to content

NeurIPS 2026 runs 6–12 December at ICC Sydney, with official satellites in Atlanta and Paris — the world's top machine-learning research conference.

NeurIPS 2026 — the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems — takes place from 6 to 12 December 2026 at the International Convention Centre (ICC) Sydney, Australia, with official satellite locations running in parallel in Atlanta, USA, and Paris, France. It is the largest and most influential gathering in machine learning, and for three decades it has been the venue where the ideas that define the field are first published — from the deep-learning breakthroughs of the 2010s to the foundation-model and agent research shaping AI today. NeurIPS is essential for machine-learning researchers and PhD students, and increasingly for industry labs that come to recruit, benchmark and read the field's frontier first.

### What's new in 2026: a distributed conference

The headline change for 2026 is the format. Rather than a single venue, NeurIPS adopts a distributed, multi-location model: Sydney is the primary host (6–12 December), with official satellite hubs in Atlanta (from 8 December) and Paris (from 9 December). The design cuts long-haul travel and its associated carbon cost, widens access for researchers who cannot reach Australia, and continues the conference's deliberate rotation across regions as the research community globalises. For attendees it means a genuine choice of hub while sharing one programme — a notable experiment in how a conference of well over 15,000 people can scale sustainably without losing its single-community character. Bringing the main event to Sydney also reflects the growing weight of the Asia-Pacific machine-learning community, which has been under-served by a conference circuit long centred on North America and Europe.

### The 2026 programme

NeurIPS combines a vast peer-reviewed main track with tutorials, invited talks, the competition track and the datasets-and-benchmarks track, plus dozens of workshops that run as miniature conferences in their own right. Coverage runs the full breadth of the field:

- Deep learning, reinforcement learning, and optimization and learning theory
- Generative and multimodal models, and the architectures behind them
- Reasoning models and agentic systems that plan, use tools and act
- Efficient and open architectures, and the maturing science of evaluation and benchmarking
- A deep strand of work on safety, alignment, interpretability and the societal impact of capable systems

The datasets-and-benchmarks and competition tracks have become especially important as the field grapples with how to measure increasingly general systems, and the workshops are often where the next year's hot topics first surface, well before they reach the main track. With tens of thousands of submissions now flowing through its review process each cycle, NeurIPS also serves as a barometer for the sheer scale and pace of machine-learning research, and its acceptance decisions shape which directions the community treats as promising.

### Who should attend and why it matters

What makes NeurIPS matter is its role as the field's centre of gravity: work presented here sets research agendas and feeds directly into the next generation of models and products. Recent editions have charted the move toward reasoning models, agentic systems, efficient and open architectures, and a maturing science of how to measure and govern capable systems. For PhD students and academic researchers it is the place to publish, present and find collaborators; for industry R&D teams and frontier labs it is where hiring, benchmarking and frontier-reading happen at once. The proceedings function as a citation backbone for the entire discipline, which is why an accepted NeurIPS paper carries outsized weight on the academic job market and in research careers. The 2026 distributed format is itself worth watching as a test of whether the world's flagship AI conference can keep its coherence while spreading across three continents, and the outcome will likely influence how other large scientific conferences approach travel, access and sustainability.

### Attending and registration

The official site at neurips.cc publishes the schedule, accepted papers, workshop list and registration for Sydney and the satellite hubs. NeurIPS registration typically fills well ahead of the event and has operated lottery or tiered allocation in high-demand years, with reduced student rates — so prospective attendees should register as early as possible and, for the Sydney venue, secure accommodation and any visa paperwork early given the December timing and the city's busy summer season. Those choosing the Atlanta or Paris satellites should confirm which sessions stream live versus run locally when planning travel, and which poster and social events are hub-specific.

results.title: NeurIPS 2026: Sydney Dates, Venue & Registration Guide | zPlatform.ai
results.text:
NeurIPS 2026: Sydney Dates, Venue & Registration Guide | zPlatform.ai

TL;DR: NeurIPS 2026 runs December 6-12, 2026, with its main event in Sydney, Australia, plus satellite conferences in Atlanta, Georgia, and Paris, France (both December 9-13). The dates on this page were already correct before this rewrite, but the venue was not: the previous version of this guide referenced New Orleans, and NeurIPS has not held its main conference there. Registration and pricing are not published yet; NeurIPS’s own 2026 pricing page states plainly that “pricing is not yet available,” and the registration portal shows it opens July 20. This guide covers what is confirmed, what 2025’s record submission year suggests is coming, and where I could not verify a claim.

I run AI Events on this site the same way I test AI SaaS tools: check the primary source before repeating a number, and say plainly when something is unconfirmed. NeurIPS is worth that discipline because it is the single most-cited AI research venue on the planet, and papers that debut there tend to show up as shipping product features 12 to 24 months later. I gave the same treatment to ICML 2026’s Seoul recap on this site, another one of the “big three” ML research conferences alongside NeurIPS and ICLR.

Below: the confirmed dates and venue, what NeurIPS has and has not published on registration and pricing, who this event is for, and what 2025’s submission numbers, awards, and a live AI-detection story in the Position Paper Track suggest about 2026. Short version: the dates were already correct on this page, the venue moved from the United States to Australia and is not yet a named building, and registration has not opened.

## Key Takeaways

- The dates were already right. NeurIPS 2026 runs December 6-12, 2026, matching the ACF field already on this post. Unlike other conferences in this guide series, no date correction was needed here.
- The venue is Sydney, Australia, not a US city. NeurIPS’s own homepage states “Main: Sydney, Australia” for 2026, with satellites in Atlanta, Georgia, and Paris, France, both December 9-13. The previous version of this page mentioned New Orleans, which is not accurate for this year.
- No specific venue building is confirmed by NeurIPS yet. Third-party event-guide sites reference ICC Sydney at Darling Harbour, the city’s obvious major convention venue, but neurips.cc had not named a specific building as of this writing. Treat that name as likely, not locked.
- Registration has not opened, and pricing is unpublished. NeurIPS’s 2026 pricing page reads “Pricing is not yet available for this conference,” and the registration portal shows registration opens July 20, with no dollar figures attached yet.
- 2025 set a high bar, and 2026 already has its own real news. NeurIPS 2025’s Main Track pulled in 21,575 valid submissions, a roughly 61% jump over 2024, with 5,290 accepted. Separately, NeurIPS 2026’s Position Paper Track already published, in June 2026, that it desk-rejected 178 submissions (18.4%) for suspected AI-generated text using a detector called Pangram, with 123 more (12.7%) required to prove human authorship. That is not a projection. It already happened.

The most useful thing I can tell you about NeurIPS 2026 right now is which parts are locked, which parts moved (the venue), and which parts are still blank. Anyone quoting you a Sydney building name or a registration fee this early is filling in blanks NeurIPS has not filled in itself.

## What Is NeurIPS 2026?

NeurIPS, the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, is the fortieth annual edition of what is widely regarded as the most important research venue in artificial intelligence and machine learning. Founded in 1987, it is run by the nonprofit Neural Information Processing Systems Foundation, per the official NeurIPS 2026 conference page. Unlike a corporate keynote conference such as NVIDIA GTC, NeurIPS is a peer-reviewed academic venue first: most of the program comes from submitted papers that pass double-blind review across the Main Track, the Datasets and Benchmarks track (recently renamed Evaluations and Datasets), and the Position Paper track, supplemented by invited talks, tutorials, competitions, and workshops.

Scale is where NeurIPS separates itself from almost every other AI event. The 2025 Main Track alone received 21,575 valid submissions and accepted 5,290 papers, a load that required 20,518 reviewers, 1,663 area chairs, and 199 senior area chairs, per NeurIPS’s own Program Committee chairs’ post-mortem. Independent press put in-person attendance at more than 20,000 researchers in San Diego, with registration selling out, continuing a trend from roughly 16,000 attendees at NeurIPS 2024 in Vancouver.

One structural detail worth knowing: NeurIPS has run a multi-site format for years, not a single host city. In 2025, San Diego was the main site, with satellites in Sydney, Atlanta, and Mexico City. For 2026, Sydney is promoted from satellite to main host, Atlanta stays on as a satellite, and Paris replaces Mexico City. If you have only ever thought of NeurIPS as “the San Diego conference,” that is why the venue on this page needed correcting rather than just the date.

## When and Where Is NeurIPS 2026?

NeurIPS 2026 runs December 6-12, 2026, with the main conference in Sydney, Australia. NeurIPS’s own dates page breaks the week down into Expo Talks on Sunday, December 6; Tutorials on Monday, December 7; the main Conference Sessions Tuesday through Thursday, December 8-10; and Workshops filling Friday and Saturday, December 11-12. Two satellite conferences run in parallel on a slightly offset schedule: Atlanta, Georgia, and Paris, France, both December 9-13, per the same official page.

Here is the correction this rewrite actually needed to make: the previous version of this page mentioned New Orleans as a “good host city” for NeurIPS, which is not accurate for 2026, and I could not find any NeurIPS edition that used New Orleans as its main site. The date field on this page, by contrast, was already correct, which is unusual in this batch of event-guide rewrites; most of the other pages needed both a date and venue fix.

One honest gap: as of this writing, NeurIPS itself had not published the name of a specific venue building in Sydney, only the city. Third-party event-tracking sites, including one independent conference guide, list the venue as ICC Sydney at Darling Harbour, and that lines up with Sydney’s only harbourside convention center built for events at this scale. I am noting that as the likely venue based on secondary sources and Sydney’s convention infrastructure, not as an official NeurIPS confirmation, because it is not one yet.

Quick facts:

| Detail | Information |
| --- | --- |
| Event | NeurIPS 2026 (40th Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems) |
| Main dates | December 6-12, 2026 |
| Main venue | Sydney, Australia (specific venue building not yet confirmed by NeurIPS; third-party sources cite ICC Sydney, Darling Harbour) |
| Satellite events | Atlanta, Georgia, and Paris, France, both December 9-13, 2026 |
| Format | In-person at each site, plus a virtual pass covering the full week |
| Conference founded | 1987 |
| 2025 submissions (Main Track, for context) | 21,575 valid submissions, 5,290 accepted (24.52% acceptance rate) |
| Registration | Not yet open; portal indicates opening July 20 |
| Pricing | Not published (“Pricing is not yet available for this conference,” per NeurIPS) |
| Full paper submission deadline (already passed) | May 6, 2026 |
| Paper author notifications | September 24, 2026 |
| Official site | neurips.cc |

## Who Should Attend NeurIPS 2026?

NeurIPS is not built for a general AI-curious audience the way a product keynote is. It is dense, peer-reviewed, and organized around research tracks rather than product announcements. You will likely get real value here if you fit one of these profiles:

- AI and ML researchers, PhD students, and research engineers who want direct exposure to the papers that will influence model architectures, training techniques, and evaluation methods over the next one to two years.
- Applied research teams inside AI labs and larger tech companies tracking what is shipping into foundation models next, since NeurIPS accepted papers have historically preceded product features like region-proposal object detection (Faster R-CNN, honored this year with the Test of Time Award) turning up across the entire computer vision industry.
- Research-adjacent policy and AI-safety practitioners, given NeurIPS’s growing Position Paper and Ethics Review tracks and its willingness to publish uncomfortable findings, like the AI-generated-text desk rejections detailed below, in public.

Here is the honest caveat: if you are coming from a business or growth role with no research background, most of NeurIPS’s core technical content, spotlight talks, and poster sessions will be hard to follow without a machine learning foundation. This is a peer-review venue wearing a conference badge, not a marketing event.

Here is a specific version of this problem worth planning around: if you budgeted for a US-based NeurIPS trip based on last year’s San Diego location, the 2026 main event has moved to Sydney with no registration fee published yet. The workaround is blunt: hold the December 6-12 week on the calendar, set a reminder for the July 20 registration window, and wait on booking flights until NeurIPS names pricing and the exact venue. Lock the dates. Don’t lock the flights.

## Program and Organizers: What Is Confirmed for NeurIPS 2026

NeurIPS does not run a single vendor keynote the way NVIDIA GTC does, so there is no headline speaker to wait on. What is already public is the organizing structure: General Chairs Hsuan-Tien Lin (National Taiwan University) and Razvan Pascanu (Google DeepMind and Mila) lead the 2026 edition, with Finale Doshi-Velez (Harvard) as Senior Program Chair and Jenna Wiens, David Rolnick, Nika Haghtalab, and Marc Deisenroth as Program Chairs, per the official 2026 organizing committee listing. Dozens more chairs run the Datasets and Benchmarks track, Position Paper track, Workshop track, Ethics Review, and the Atlanta and Paris satellites specifically.

Not published yet: any invited-talk lineup, a workshop list (acceptance notifications go out July 11, 2026), or a session-by-session agenda. NeurIPS’s own site says “more information on NeurIPS 2026 will be available soon,” worth taking at face value rather than guessing names this far out.

One piece of real, dated news worth flagging: NeurIPS’s Main Program is running a voluntary AI-Assisted Reviewing Experiment this cycle, built into OpenReview, randomly assigning consenting reviewers to one of three conditions per paper: no LLM assistance, open-ended LLM assistance, or structured LLM assistance, with area chairs blind to which condition produced which review. It is IRB-approved through the University of Texas at Austin and framed explicitly as a study, not a policy change, per the official experiment page. Outside this opt-in study, NeurIPS still bans other LLM use in reviewing, with violations leading to desk rejection.

## What Themes Will NeurIPS 2026 Cover?

NeurIPS has not published a 2026 session catalog broken down by topic, so most of what follows is a precedent-based read on 2025, not a confirmed 2026 program. But one piece of this section is not a projection at all: it already happened, and it is one of the more unusual data points in this entire event-guide series.

Real 2026 news: an AI-generated-text detection episode in the Position Paper Track. In June 2026, the track’s chairs published a blog post explaining that they partnered with an AI-detection company called Pangram to audit submissions against a policy requiring papers to be “substantially human-written.” The results: 178 submissions (18.4% of the track) were desk-rejected without the right to appeal, and another 123 (12.7%) were told to submit a documented “pre-AI, post-AI, final” version history proving human authorship or face the same fate, by a June 15, 2026 deadline. The chairs’ own comparison table showed submissions flagged at a 90%+ Pangram score jumped from 11.9% in 2025 to 42.7% in 2026, and from under 1% to 9.3% in the separate Evaluations and Datasets track over the same period. Whatever else 2026 ends up covering, “how peer review copes with LLM-written submissions” is already a defining, sourced story of this year, not a guess.

Precedent from 2025: what actually won awards. NeurIPS 2025’s Best Paper Awards went to seven papers (four best, including one from the Datasets and Benchmarks track, plus three runner-ups), spanning diffusion model theory, self-supervised reinforcement learning, LLM attention mechanisms and reasoning, online learning theory, neural scaling laws, and language-model diversity benchmarking, per NeurIPS’s own Best Paper Awards announcement. One winner, “Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models,” examined how similar today’s LLMs sound to each other, a theme likely to recur given how much of the field now runs on a handful of foundation models. The 2025 Test of Time Award, recognizing decade-old research that has held up, went to the 2015 Faster R-CNN paper, cited more than 56,700 times and still underlying large parts of modern object detection.

If 2025’s trajectory holds, expect continued heavy volume in LLM reasoning, evaluation methodology, and generative model theory, plus a Position Paper track now shaped directly by the AI-detection story above. None of that is a confirmed session list, just a pattern read off the most recent year.

## NeurIPS 2026 Registration and Ticket Pricing

NeurIPS has not published registration pricing for 2026. The official 2026 pricing page states directly: “Pricing is not yet available for this conference.” The registration portal shows registration is “currently closed” and opens July 20, with no dollar amounts attached yet.

For budgeting context only, here is a historically typical NeurIPS registration structure, not a confirmed 2026 figure: registration splits by affiliation type (full-time student, academic, non-academic/industrial), and a widely cited 2023 breakdown put fees at roughly $375 for students, $800 for academics, and $1,000 for industry attendees. That figure is three years old and pre-dates NeurIPS’s continued attendance growth, so treat it as a rough historical floor, not a 2026 estimate. Physical registration has historically included the virtual pass at no extra cost, with a cheaper virtual-only pass also available.

Cancellation and visa-related refund policies for NeurIPS 2025 were specific: a full refund applied if you canceled before a set date in November, dropping to no refund after that, with a separate accommodation letting visa-denied attendees convert to a virtual registration and get the price difference refunded. I would expect 2026 to publish a similar structure once pricing goes live, since NeurIPS has run some version of this policy for years, but the exact 2026 dates are not out yet.
